newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Descending Russian spacecraft burns up, parts sink.
newsitem.headline: Descending Russian spacecraft burns up, parts sink.

text.p: A descending unmanned Russian cargo spacecraft burned up on Wednesday morning in the atmosphere but some parts fell in the Pacific Ocean, a mission control spokesman said.
"The Progress M-33 spacecraft entered the upper layer of the Earth's atmosphere and burned up there at 6.23 a.m. (0323 GMT)," the spokesman told Reuters by telephone.

"We think some parts of the craft, about 200 kg of metal, fell into the Pacific Ocean at a distance of 3,150 km (1,970 miles) east of Wellington, New Zealand," the spokesman said, adding that none of the parts that fell into the sea were radioactive.
Russian space authorities decided to let the Progress M-33 cargo vessel burn up after it had failed to dock with the Mir orbiting station.
The Progress M-33 has been in orbit since November 1996 and delivered water, food, air and fuel to the Mir crew.
It undocked from Mir on February 6 to make way for a Soyuz TM-25 craft which brought a replacement crew to the orbiting station, but several attempts to link it back to Mir failed.
Russia plans to launch next cargo space craft to the Mir at the end of March, but the launch, already delayed several times, may be dealyed further, officials said.
